references.text: Joseph gave advice to Pharaoh, and Pharaoh listened to him and acted according to his words, just as Moses listened to his father-in-law Jethro and did all that he said.
Rehoboam refused to listen to the people's advice, unlike Moses who was willing to listen to his father-in-law's wise counsel and act accordingly.
Micaiah delivered the Lord's word, and the king was urged to listen. Moses demonstrated humility by listening to advice from his father-in-law.
A wise man hears and increases his learning. Moses, who was a wise leader, listened to Jethro's counsel.
The apostles chose seven men to handle practical tasks so they could focus on prayer and the ministry of the word. This resembles the structure Jethro proposed for Moses.
Both verses confirm Moses' total obedience as a consistent principle in his service.
